es: Evaluar un rumor del huerto combinando pistas, marcadores epistémicos y evidenciales, y defender la conclusión ante una objeción.

teaching.en: My first hypothesis is that, in all likelihood, a person took the vegetables.

prompt.es: Resuelve el caso del huerto (unas 110 palabras): pistas, dos hipótesis y objeción.

answer.text: Evidently, someone entered the garden last night, because there are footprints in the soil. The gate was unlocked, so it appears that anyone could come in. Apparently, a neighbour saw a man with a bag at dawn, but she has not confirmed it, and the rumour that a member took the vegetables is allegedly based on nothing. In all likelihood, a stranger did it. Conceivably, it was a member, but that is doubtful. Carlos, that is a fair objection, but the gate was unlocked, so we cannot rule out a stranger, and we should not jump to conclusions.

Evidently, somebody came in during the night: the footprints in the soil are clear. The gate was unlocked, so it seems that anyone could enter. Apparently, a neighbour saw a man with a bag at dawn, but nobody has confirmed it, and the rumour about a member has no proof. In all likelihood, it was a stranger. Conceivably, a member did it, but that is unlikely. I understand your objection, Carlos, but the gate was unlocked, so we cannot rule out a stranger. We should not jump to conclusions.

The footprints in the soil show evidently that someone was here last night. It appears that the gate was unlocked, so anybody could come in. Reportedly, a neighbour saw a man with a bag at dawn, although she is not sure, and a rumour says that a member took the vegetables, allegedly without any proof. Probably, a stranger took them. Possibly it was a member, but that is doubtful. That is a fair point, Carlos, but we cannot rule out a stranger, so let us not jump to conclusions.

feedback.es: La respuesta completa clasifica las pistas (directa, inferencia, segunda mano), propone una hipótesis fuerte y otra débil y responde a la objeción con un dato y prudencia.

origin.text: Caso: han desaparecido verduras del huerto comunitario. Pistas: (1) huellas en la tierra; (2) la puerta estaba sin cerrar; (3) una vecina dice que vio a un hombre con una bolsa al amanecer; (4) corre el rumor de que un socio se las llevó. Carlos objeta: «It must have been a member; the gate is always locked.» Escribe unas 110 palabras: analiza las pistas (evidently, it appears that, apparently, allegedly), propón dos hipótesis con distinto grado de certeza y responde a la objeción.
